course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Globalization
unit.description: Study how technology, disease, and environmental change reshaped the world, how the global economy and culture developed, and how people and institutions responded to globalization.

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 9.8 key concept: new international organizations formed to maintain world peace and facilitate cooperation
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing international organizations after 1945
stimulusBlocks.text:
The United Nations, founded in 1945, sent peacekeepers to conflicts from Cyprus to Cambodia, and its World Health Organization coordinated campaigns against disease. Two institutions planned in 1944, the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, lent money to countries for stability and development, often requiring governments to cut spending in return.

Nongovernmental organizations also grew. Amnesty International, founded in 1961, campaigned for political prisoners, and Doctors Without Borders, founded in 1971, sent medical teams to war zones and disaster areas.

questions.prompt: Amnesty International and Doctors Without Borders were similar in that both
choices: were private groups working across borders
were founded in 1945 alongside the UN
were agencies of the United Nations
lent money to governments for development
questions.explanation: Both are private groups acting internationally.
choiceExplanations: Both are private groups acting internationally.
They were founded in 1961 and 1971.
They are independent of the UN.
The IMF and World Bank lend money.
questions.distinguisher: They often work alongside UN agencies but are independent of the UN.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 9.8 key concept: regional and global organizations facilitated trade and cooperation
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing regional and trade organizations, 1957–2002
stimulusBlocks.text:
Six Western European states formed a common market in 1957. It grew into the European Union in 1993, and in 1999 many members adopted a shared currency, the euro. Members gave up some control over trade and borders in exchange for economic growth and lasting peace.

Other regions formed their own organizations, including the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in 1967 and the African Union in 2002. In 1995, the World Trade Organization replaced an earlier agreement on tariffs and began settling trade disputes among its members.

questions.prompt: The passage best supports which claim about organizations after 1950?
choices: Regional cooperation spread to many parts of the world
Only Europe formed regional organizations
Trade organizations stopped settling disputes
The euro was adopted by every nation
questions.explanation: Europe, Southeast Asia, and Africa all formed organizations.
choiceExplanations: Europe, Southeast Asia, and Africa all formed organizations.
ASEAN and the African Union show otherwise.
The WTO began settling disputes in 1995.
Only some EU members adopted the euro.
questions.distinguisher: Europe led, but Southeast Asia and Africa formed their own organizations.
